stem:
Lalit hears that this year's collection is $150\%$ of last year's base of ₹$200$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Treat $150\%$ as more than the base after ignoring which amount was chosen as the $100\%$ base.
Say that collecting ₹$300$ is what creates the $150\%$ reading, instead of $150\%$ of the base giving ₹$300$.
$150\%$ means $1.5$ times the chosen base, so ₹$300$, which exceeds the ₹$200$ base.
Use "$150\%$ exceeds the base" to decide whether a fraction is greater than $1$ when no percentage base was chosen.

teacher.key_rationale: A percentage greater than $100$ means the quantity exceeds the chosen base: $150\%$ of ₹$200$ is ₹$300$. Dropping the base, reversing amount and percent, or stretching to bare fractions all miss that hinge.
